title: User Trust on an Explainable AI-based Medical Diagnosis Support System
venue: Proceedings of Workshop on Trust and Reliance in AI-Human Teams at CHI 2022 (TRAIT at CHI 2022)
extended_summary:
This paper investigates how medical professionals trust and rely on an explainable AI system for chest X-ray diagnosis. The authors focus on the gap between technical model performance and user trust, asking whether providing causal explanations for a diagnosis can improve agreement with the system and calibrate reliance.

The intervention is an explainable AI-based medical diagnosis support system that predicts three emergency-department prognosis classes from chest X-rays and also outputs 13 causal anomaly probabilities as explanations. Users could view the image, inspect the model’s prediction and explanation, and then adjust the explanation probabilities via a slider if they disagreed. Trust was measured in two ways: observed trust (agreement with predictions and alignment with explanations) and self-reported trust using a five-item Likert questionnaire.

The study was conducted online with five radiology/clinic professionals from institutions in Germany. Results showed a 46.4% agreement rate with the model’s final predictions, while self-reported trust was moderate (median score 3.2/5). Users tended to align with the model’s explanations more than with its final predictions, suggesting some over-reliance on explanations and mixed trust overall. The authors conclude that explanation-based XAI alone did not fully calibrate trust, and that better communication of model uncertainty and more user training may be needed.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a small, peer-reviewed user study with qualitative and correlational elements, not an RCT or QED. The methodology is clear, but the sample size is very small (n=5), limiting credibility for causal claims.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests an unclear-to-modest impact on decision support behavior, with 46.4% agreement and signs of over-reliance but no intervention effect size on educational outcomes. Because the study is in a medical setting and primarily measures trust/calibration, the practical impact is informative but limited.

interventions.use_case: An explainable AI-based medical diagnosis support system for chest X-ray interpretation, showing model predictions plus causal explanations that users can edit before final diagnosis output.

finding.finding_summary: This study focused on user trust, agreement, and reliance when professionals interacted with an explainable diagnosis support system rather than on patient or learning outcomes. The main observed-behavior metric was agreement with the model’s final prediction: radiologists agreed in 46.4% of cases (n=5, 6 images each), despite the model achieving 74.12% accuracy on the test set. Explanations were often aligned with users’ edited causal explanations, but the system also showed signs of over-reliance on some incorrect explanations, indicating mixed effects on decision support behavior.
finding.measure: Agreement rate with model prediction; alignment of user-edited causal explanations with model explanations; self-reported trust questionnaire
